text:
marta: Heads-up — ran the kernel-pick autotune job against a couple of arm64 hosts (Graviton2 + Mac M1 pool) and short-seq p99 jumped ~12% after the last autotune pass. Noticed it only shows up for seq <= 64, batch=1.

juan: Oof. Which kernel got picked?

marta: We enabled RUNTIME_KPICK_DEBUG=1 on a canary. Logs show picks like: `sgemm_unroll128` on aarch64, whereas x86 kept `sgemm_tiled`.

omar: Could be unroll overhead for tiny matrices. bank conflicts / cache thrash on L1 on arm cores are brutal for those tile sizes.

marta: Exact log snippet:
```
KPICK: model=llama-13b seq=32 batch=1 device=aarch64 node=grv2-10
CHOSEN=sgemm_unroll128 reason="est_latency:3.2 < alt:3.4 (mem_est penalty 0.9)"
KERNEL_METRICS est_cycles=1234 est_regs=80 heur_flags=UNROLL32|USE_PREFETCH
```

elin: perfbot ran microbenchmarks? @perfbot any profile traces attached? :eyes:

perfbot: automated profile attached (uploaded). Summary: p50 unchanged, p95 +9%, p99 +12% for seq<=64 on aarch64. Flame graph points to kernel dispatch + first-block GEMM path.

juan: Did autotune change the cost model weights recently? The unroll path probably got slightly lower estimated latency due to new memory throughput numbers.

marta: Yes — last commit (autotune/weights#42) bumped mem_throughput for arm by +15%. That made unrolled kernels look better in the heuristic.

omar: Can reproduce on my M1 dev machine with `--workload seq=32 batch=1`. Repro script I used: 
```bash
./dev/repro_kpick.sh --model llama-13b --seq 32 --batch 1 --device aarch64 
# then: grep KPICK out/runtime.log | tail -n 20
```

dave: Any quick mitigation? We can force the previous pick for short seqs until we fix model weights.

marta: I pushed a small runtime flag: `KPICK_FORCE_LEGACY_SHORTSEQ=1` — sets a seq threshold to prefer tiled kernels for seq<=64. Patch is in my branch marta/kpick-shortseq-fix.

elin: Nice. Can we instead tweak the cost model instead of ad-hoc flag? The unroll might still be better for some threads.

juan: Agree. Short-term flag + a follow-up autotune sweep limited to seq bins {8,16,32,64} on arm64 to recalibrate mem_throughput is safest. We should also log the KPICK_REASON in metrics for aggregation.

marta: I added KPICK_REASON -> prometheus label in the branch. Example: `kpick_kernel="sgemm_unroll128", kpick_reason="est_latency_delta:-0.2,mem_adj:+15%"`

omar: If we expose that, we can run a nightly job to count which kernel wins per seq/batch/devtype. That should highlight regressions automatically.

perfbot: Suggested alert: if kernel distribution changes by >20% for any seq bin in 24h, create a perf-alert ticket. I can wire that up.

juan: Also, add a debug env `RUNTIME_KPICK_DUMP=1` that emits a one-line JSON per request (only in debug builds) with fields: kernel, reason, est_times, flags. Helps quick grepping without full logs.

marta: Done locally. Example line: 
`{"ts":1768745300, "kernel":"sgemm_unroll128", "reason":"mem_boost", "seq":32, "batch":1, "device":"aarch64"}`

elin: For the follow-up: please include microbench runs that exercise int8/quant paths too. Sometimes quant kernels have different cache behavior and the pick changes.

marta: Will run: seq bins {8,16,32,64,128} x batch 1,2,4 x quant {fp16,int8}. Uploading CSV to the canary workspace shortly.

dave: Thanks — once we have the new autotune numbers and KPICK telemetry, we can remove the force flag. Also add a short playbook: how to turn KPICK_FORCE_LEGACY_SHORTSEQ on/off per cluster.

marta: Yep. I opened issue #4221 with reproduction steps, logs, patch link, and perfbot alert recipe. Assigning to @juan for autotune sweep.

juan: I'll kick off sweep tonight and post results in this thread. If anyone wants to reproduce locally, use Omar's script + set `RUNTIME_KPICK_DEBUG=1` and `RUNTIME_KPICK_DUMP=1`.

omar: Repro confirmed, sending flame graphs + small perf note in the issue.

marta: Thanks all. TL;DR: autotune weight change exposed a short-seq regression on arm64; we have a short-term flag, telemetry to track winners, and an autotune follow-up. :white_check_mark:
